claim: With one uniformly random screen of six, 55.1% of reference-positive Malawi households would be missed
statistical_definition: M_1 = mean over K>0 of C(6-K,1)/C(6,1)
caveat: Conditional on six observed 30-day windows; not annual; random-window benchmark

claim: With two random screens, 31.9% of Malawi reference-positive households missed
caveat: As above

claim: With three random screens, 18.2% of Malawi reference-positive households missed
caveat: As above

claim: Liberia: 69.6% / 47.5% / 30.7% missed with 1 / 2 / 3 random screens
caveat: Only 33% of frame complete; 47 villages

claim: Over the whole Malawi frame, M_1 lies in 50.8-59.3% whatever the missing windows were
statistical_definition: min/max M_1 over all binary completions
caveat: No assumptions on missing windows; observed labels taken as correct

claim: Over the whole Liberia frame, M_1 lies in 39.8-78.6%
statistical_definition: min/max M_1 over all completions
caveat: Weak identification

claim: Allowing 5% of observed labels to be wrong widens Malawi M_1 range to 39.6-65.0%
statistical_definition: min/max M_1 with shared budget of 82 flips and arbitrary missing
caveat: 5% is not an estimated error rate

claim: Allowing 5% label error widens Liberia M_1 range to 25.1-82.5%
statistical_definition: as above, 40 flips
caveat: 5% is not an estimated error rate

claim: Single imputations (all missing negative/positive) are not the sharp endpoints
statistical_definition: naive values strictly inside sharp range
caveat: Denominator changes with completion

claim: In Malawi, Jan-Feb is the best single window in 2020 (13.6% missed)
statistical_definition: min over 4 windows of share of reference-positive negative in that window
uncertainty_type: Selection stability: Jan-Feb chosen in 100% of 2000 bootstrap re-selections
caveat: In-sample selection

claim: Frozen Jan-Feb window missed 21.6% of Malawi reference-positive households in 2021 vs 59.8% for a random window
statistical_definition: frozen-slot missed share in 2021
caveat: Two adjacent pandemic-era years; not causal

claim: Matched Malawi households: frozen Jan-Feb missed 20.2% in 2021 vs 59.8% random
statistical_definition: as above, households complete in both years
caveat: Same caveats

claim: Liberia: 2020-selected Mar-Apr window did not clearly outperform a random window in 2021
statistical_definition: frozen vs random difference
uncertainty_type: Difference -5.7 pp (-26.9 to 14.1); selection unstable (62% bootstrap)
caveat: Uninformative; very small n (13 matched positives)

claim: Most reference-positive households are positive in only 1-3 of 6 windows
statistical_definition: distribution of K among complete
caveat: Six windows only

claim: Best fixed two-window Malawi schedule (Jan-Feb + Mar-Apr) missed 6.5% in 2020
statistical_definition: missed share for fixed subset
caveat: Winner's curse; exploratory

claim: Severe hunger (HHS>=4) is near-degenerate
statistical_definition: K distribution at threshold 4
caveat: Do not analyse severe-only

claim: MAR-type IPW leaves estimates almost unchanged
statistical_definition: IPW-weighted M_m
caveat: MAR given 7 baseline covariates is untestable

claim: Jan-Feb screen missed 38.3% of Malawi reference positives vs 59.3% for a random window (difference -20.9 pp)
statistical_definition: missed share of fixed window minus mean missed share of a random window
caveat: Lead timing result; window chosen on Jul 2019 - Jun 2020; investigators had seen these outcomes

claim: No uniquely best window: in Jul 2020 - Jun 2021 the best observed window was Nov-Dec (37.6% missed); Jan-Feb (+0.8 pp) and Sep-Oct (+6.0 pp) were not separable from it
statistical_definition: paired difference in missed share, window minus best observed window
uncertainty_type: 95% village bootstrap: Jan-Feb -9.8 to 12.1; Sep-Oct -5.5 to 17.8 pp
caveat: The best observed window is selected in the same data, so its advantage over others is optimistic

claim: September-February windows had lower mean missed shares than March-August windows in every Malawi horizon
statistical_definition: mean missed share of Sep-Feb windows minus mean of Mar-Aug windows
population: Aggarwal Malawi and World Bank Malawi horizons
caveat: Suggested after window results were known; designs unbalanced except the three six-window Aggarwal horizons

claim: Frozen best pair (Nov-Dec + Jan-Feb) missed 15.0% vs 36.4% for a random pair
statistical_definition: missed share with two fixed windows minus random pair
caveat: Pair chosen on Jul 2019 - Jun 2020

claim: Liberia: the calendar window (Jul-Aug) did not outperform random (3.7 pp)
statistical_definition: fixed minus random missed share
caveat: Small sample (secondary country)

claim: World Bank Malawi 2021 (five rounds): best observed round R8 Mar 2021 (25.9% missed); R7 Jan was 5.1 pp worse

caveat: FIES item 7, not HHS; district clusters approximate

claim: Failed transfer: the round chosen on 2020 (R1 Jun 2020) missed 47.8% in 2021 vs 35.1% random
statistical_definition: frozen-round missed share minus random-round
